issues.description: Field name mismatch for Ride.abbreviation: The UML in problem_statement.md declares an attribute named 'abbreviation' of type char (and the exercise instructions require public getters for all attributes). The solution implementation (src/de/tum/in/ase/Ride.java) declares a char field named 'shortName' and provides a getter getShortName(). The template Ride.java is empty but the UML is the specification students will follow. This naming inconsistency (abbreviation vs shortName / getAbbreviation() vs getShortName()) can confuse students about the exact attribute name and expected getter to implement and may lead to mismatches with tests or grading that expect UML-consistent identifiers.
issues.suggestedFix: Align identifiers with the UML: rename the field 'shortName' to 'abbreviation' (type char) in Ride, rename the constructor parameter accordingly, and provide a getter getAbbreviation(). Update all subclasses and constructors that pass or reference this parameter (e.g., LaunchedDropdownTower, LaunchedRollerCoaster) to use the name 'abbreviation' to keep parameter order and names consistent with the UML and exercise instructions.

issues.description: Concept: the Ride class attribute that holds the ride's single-character identifier. In the problem statement/UML (problem_statement.md lines 21-24) the attribute is named 'abbreviation' of type char. In the solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/in/ase/Ride.java) the same concept is implemented as the field 'shortName' (private char shortName) and exposed via getShortName(), with the constructor parameter also named shortName. This naming mismatch between 'abbreviation' (UML/problem) and 'shortName' (solution) can confuse students mapping UML attributes to class fields, constructor parameters and expected getter names (they may expect a getAbbreviation() and a constructor parameter named abbreviation).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the identifier names so the UML/problem and implementation match. Either: (a) rename the solution field 'shortName' -> 'abbreviation', rename the constructor parameter to 'abbreviation' and rename getShortName() -> getAbbreviation(); or (b) update the UML/problem statement to use 'shortName' instead of 'abbreviation'. Prefer option (a) to match the UML as specified in the exercise.
